lectures.title: Fibonnaci Series using Divide and Conquer

cues.en: All right.
In this lecture we are going to look at how can we solve Fibonacci series using divide and conquer.
Now we have talked about Fibonacci series in recursion section.
So here I'm just going to bring the same definition and show you how this is working.
Then I'll show you how we solve it using divide and conquer approach.
So in this case the definition of Fibonacci series is like this.
It's a series of numbers in which each number is the sum of the two preceding numbers, and first two
numbers, by definition are zero and one.
Now, if you calculate the third number, we have to sum up these two numbers zero plus one is going
to be one.
Then if we calculate the fourth number we have to sum up previous two numbers which is one plus one
is two.
Then if you calculate the fifth number it's going to be one plus two which is three.
Then it continues like this until infinity.
So this means that we can write this series like this.
So the equation can be like this.
So Fibonacci of n is equal to Fibonacci of n minus one plus Fibonacci of n minus two.
So in this case for example for 21 it's going to be eight plus 13.
So that's how the Fibonacci series looks like.
So let's see how we can solve this using divide and conquer approach.
So here I'm just going to put the series like this.
Let's say we want to find out Fibonacci for.
So this means that this is the fourth number in the Fibonacci series.
And it starts from the zero.
Now to be able to calculate this using divide and conquer approach, we have to divide this problem
into two parts.
So according to the definition, we have said that this number is equal to the sum of the previous two
numbers.
So we can write this problem like this.
So we can divide this problem into two subproblems which is Fibonacci of three and Fibonacci of two.
Then we can go ahead and calculate these ones.
Now in case of Fibonacci of three we can divide it into two parts.
We need to calculate the Fibonacci of two and Fibonacci of one.
And in case of Fibonacci two, we can divide it further with the Fibonacci of one and Fibonacci of zero.
Now for this Fibonacci two.
Also, we can divide it into two parts.
It's going to be like this Fibonacci of one and Fibonacci of zero.
Now until we reach this part, we cannot divide it further, because according to the definition, the
Fibonacci of one is one and Fibonacci of zero is zero.
So from here we can calculate Fibonacci of one and zero and combine it to the Fibonacci of two, then
we know Fibonacci of two, and we know Fibonacci of one.
And we are going to combine it to the Fibonacci of three.
And it continues like this.
So as you can see, we can easily divide this problem into subproblems, then solve some problems and
combine them together.
So this means that Fibonacci series can be solved using the divide and conquer approach.
So as we did before, the recursive solution for Fibonacci is going to be like this.
So take into account that Fibonacci series is only for positive integer numbers.
So that's why over here we have a base case.
If it is less than zero, we are just going to return this message.
Otherwise if it is zero, we are returning zero.
If it is one, we are returning one.
And if this is not the case, we are dividing this problem into subproblems, which is n minus one and
n minus two, and continuing until we reach 0 or 1.
So after reaching there, we are going to combine these subproblems together to get the final solution.
So as I mentioned, we have already solved this problem before.
So I'm not going to go to the details how this is working.
So if you want to see the details you can refer back to recursion section.
So here I just wanted to show you that it can be solved in divide and conquer manner.
So hopefully everything is clear.
